version.changelog:
web-browser v0.2.2

- Documentation updates across multiple guides and the main skill file for clarity and accuracy.
- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.
- Clarified backend detection logic and selection process in all documentation.
- No feature or logic changes; all updates are non-functional and documentation-focused.

llm.summary: This browser helper openly supports UI testing, but it also mandates broad credential discovery, automated token extraction, and persistent secret storage, which needs careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: The UI-testing purpose is coherent, but the credential workflow goes well beyond browser assistance by checking local/project/secret stores, issuing or refreshing tokens, extracting token values from authenticated pages, persisting them, and handing them to downstream commands.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Sensitive actions are framed as mandatory hard stops, including storing every issued credential, preferring backend extraction over user copy, and routing Microsoft logins through GitHub SSO, with limited explicit per-action consent or opt-out.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is mostly documentation plus one Playwright CDP script; it instructs dynamic npm/npx Playwright setup and MCP registration, but metadata and static scan do not show hidden install hooks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reusing a real logged-in Chrome session and piercing closed shadow DOM can be legitimate for debugging, but combined with credential extraction it gives the agent access to sensitive authenticated page state.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill mandates writing secrets into keyrings, Vault, GitHub secrets, local CLI config files, .env files, and skill data; it also includes troubleshooting commands that kill Chrome processes and may delete a Playwright profile directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to help issue, refresh, extract, store, and reuse credentials from browser sessions. Before using it, require explicit approval for each secret lookup, token extraction, storage destination, scope expansion, SSO choice, and any profile deletion or process-kill recovery step.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: The scanner's credential-discovery concern is supported by artifact text requiring checks of skill data, project memory, .env files, Vault, and GitHub secrets before browser issuance; this is broader than a narrowly scoped browser helper.
[SSD-3] expected: Credential acquisition is part of the declared credential-issue workflow, but the artifacts make extraction and persistence mandatory, which creates a material Review concern rather than a clean purpose-aligned note.
[PE3] expected: References to keyrings, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.oci/config, Vault, GitHub secrets, and .env files are real and expected for credential persistence, but the breadth and mandatory retention are high-impact.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The concerns about missing consent checkpoints are supported: the skill directs backend token extraction from page snapshots and persistence before handoff, without requiring an explicit per-secret approval step.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad trigger phrases such as browser test, open login screen, service credential, issue token, and scope expansion could activate this skill in sensitive authentication contexts.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The artifact does mandate GitHub SSO first for Microsoft-gated services, which can override identity-provider choice and should be user-directed.
